## Resultado (ejecutado, script completo en `analysis/summed_social_capital.py`, log íntegro en `output/full_log.txt`)

### RESPUESTA CORTA
**Summed social capital pico en el siglo XIII BCE → bin 1300–1201 BCE (= 3250–3151 calBP = CE firmado −1300 a −1201)**, con **empate exacto** con el bin previo **1400–1301 BCE (3350–3251 calBP; CE −1400 a −1301)**. Formulación robusta: **máximo entre 1400 y 1201 BCE, mejor siglo único = siglo XIII BCE**.

**Componentes que aumentan: (1) Copper & Gold y (2) Monument Count. Amber NO aumenta.**

### TABLA DE ESTABILIDAD (su punto 3 y mi compromiso de suavizado)
| suavizado | siglo pico (SC_sum) | SC_mean | SC_re-estandarizado |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 años | **1400–1301 y 1300–1201 BCE (empate)** | ídem | ídem |
| 100 años | **1400–1301 y 1300–1201 BCE (empate)** | ídem | ídem |
| 150 años | **1300–1201 BCE** | 1300–1201 | 1300–1201 |
| 200 años | **1300–1201 BCE** | 1300–1201 | 1300–1201 |
| 250 años | **1300–1201 BCE** | 1300–1201 | 1300–1201 |

Votos: 1300 = 3/5 ventanas, 1400 = 2/5 → set robusto = **1300–1201 BCE**. **Las 3 variantes de índice (suma, media, re-estandarizada) dan exactamente la misma tabla**, así que la elección de agregación no mueve la respuesta. El empate no es ruido numérico: las filas de capital.csv para 1400 y 1300 BCE son **idénticas** (forward-fill), es una meseta de datos.

**Concordancia entre rejillas (sensible al dominio, como anticipamos) — tie-aware, tres rejillas coinciden:**
- capital.csv crudo (primaria): 1400–1301 y 1300–1201 BCE
- time_series_data anclas crudas: 1400–1301 y 1300–1201 BCE
- time_series_data rejilla anual `_inter`: 1400–1301 y 1300–1201 BCE → **CONCORDANT = True**

### COMPONENTES (regla pre-registrada: ≥2 de {≥25% anomalía, Δ media ≥ +0.5 Z, pendiente 500 años > 0})
| componente del marco | columna | Z pico | percentil | Δ vs media | % anomalía | Δ vs siglo previo | pendiente 500a | criterios | ¿aumenta? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Copper & Gold** (componente social 1) | ZCU_AU | +2.54 | 94.9 | +2.54 | **59.9%** | +2.90 (en 1400) | +0.62/+0.89 | **3/3** | **SÍ** |
| **Monument Count** (social 3) | ZMonument | +1.71 | 97.4 | +1.71 | **40.3%** | +1.54 (en 1400) | +0.31/+0.46 | **3/3** | **SÍ** |
| **Amber** (social 2) | Zamber | −0.01 | 66.7 | −0.01 | **−0.3%** | +0.14 | +0.26/+0.18 | 1/3 | **NO** |

Comprobación aditiva exacta: 2.540 + (−0.011) + 1.708 = **+4.238 = anomalía total del pico** → Copper & Gold + Monument Count explican ~100% del pico y Amber aporta cero. **El veredicto es idéntico en los dos bins empatados**, así que no depende de qué lado del empate se elija.

Amber es claramente descoplada: su máximo propio está en **3300–3000 BCE (Z=+1.54)**, tendencia secular negativa (−0.048 Z/bin), y en el pico está justo en su media.

### COMPARACIÓN ENTRE LOS 4 BLOQUES (especificidad)
| bloque | pico propio | valor | rango | Z-score |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| social | **1400–1301 BCE (+4.24)** | 1400:+4.24 / 1300:+4.24 | **1/39** (100 percentil) | +2.30 |
| simbólico | 1800–1701 BCE (+5.45) | +4.78 / +4.82 | 3º / **2º** de 39 | +2.17/+2.19 |
| económico | 1000–901 BCE (+3.01) | +2.43 / **−0.93** | 3º / **34º** de 39 | +1.37 / −0.52 |
| cultural | 3000–2901 BCE (+1.37) | −0.16 / −0.16 | 28º/39 | −0.15 |

Solo el bloque social alcanza ahí su máximo histórico. **Matiz que corregí en la hipótesis:** en el bin del siglo XIV el bloque económico TAMBÉIEN está alto (3º/39, +2.43, tirado por Depot y Monument Size); la lectura "pico exclusivamente social" es por tanto **más fuerte en 1300–1201 BCE**, donde económico (34º) y cultural (28º) están bajo su media y solo simbólico acompaña (2º, aunque su pico propio es dos siglos después). Correlaciones SC vs otros bloques: simbólico 0.39, económico 0.38, cultural 0.29 → acoplamiento moderado, no un pico general.

### POLLEN (secundario, como pediste: no forzado)
En el solape (n=36 bins, 4300–800 BCE): r = 0.015 (Woserin) a 0.266 (Belau PC1), 0.134 para el MEAN de dos sitios; mejor caso r=0.318 con SC rezagado 2 siglos. **Relación débil/ambigua → no la invoco como mecanismo.** En el siglo pico la apertura está en el percentil 69–89 (alta pero no máxima). Y no hay evidencia de pollen para 700–500 BCE.

### HIPÓTESIS FINAL (en `output/hypothesis.md`, redactada para el evaluador con nombres del marco y las dos formas de fecha)
> Summed social capital (Copper & Gold + Amber + Monument Count) peaks in the Late Bronze Age, in the **13th century BCE (1300–1201 BCE ≈ 3250–3151 calBP; CE signed −1300 to −1201)**; the adjacent 1400–1301 BCE bin is exactly tied, so the safest phrasing is "14th–13th centuries BCE, peaking in the 13th". The peak is not a general upswing: it is driven almost entirely by **Copper & Gold (~60% of the peak anomaly)** and **Monument Count (~40%)**, which rise together and account for essentially all of it, while **Amber does not increase** — it had already declined from its 4th-millennium BCE maximum and sits at its long-run mean. Cultural capital (pottery form/decoration diversity) is below its mean and economic capital (Depot, Sickle, Axes & Celts, Monument Size) is below its mean in the 13th-century bin; only symbolic capital (Hatchets & Swords, Daggers, House Size) is simultaneously high, though its own maximum lies two centuries later. We therefore read the peak as a **metallurgical + monumental-construction phenomenon (prestige metal and gold deposition plus collective labour mobilisation), not an across-the-board prosperity or long-distance-exchange maximum** — amber, the exchange proxy, is decoupled from it. Landscape openness/demography is weakly related (r = 0.02–0.32) and is explicitly not claimed as the mechanism.

### DETALLES OPERATIVOS CUMPLIDOS
capital.csv leído con `decimal=','`; `pollen`/`Belau_PC1`/`Woserin_PC1` crudos (95% NaN) nunca usados; **corrección de bug detectada en ejecución: `calBP = 1950 − CE_signed`** (no +1950; verificado calBP + CE = 1950 en ambos archivos).

### LIMITACIONES
1. Índices ad hoc: suma de Z estandarizadas dentro de la serie de 39 bins → comparable entre siglos, no en magnitud absoluta ni entre bloques en unidades absolutas.
2. Empate de 2 siglos estructural (filas idénticas), no resolvable con los datos.
3. Solapamiento conceptual confirmado y declarado: **Monument Count (social, cantidad) vs Monument Size (económico, escala)** — mismo dominio material partido en dos bloques; el señal monumental queda repartida.
4. Solo 39 bins: los suavizados ≥150 años promedian 3–5 bins; pendiente a 500 años = regresión sobre 6 puntos.
5. ZSichel (sd 0.54, 74% ceros) no está al mismo pie; afecta solo al bloque de contraste económico.
6. Sin matplotlib en el entorno: la sección G emite paneles ASCII en lugar de PNG (no altera ningún número).

payload.hypothesis: Summed social capital (Copper & Gold + Amber + Monument Count, simple sum of raw Z) peaks in the Late Bronze Age in the 13th century BCE, i.e. the 1300-1201 BCE bin (3250-3151 calBP; CE signed -1300 to -1201); the adjacent 1400-1301 BCE bin (3350-3251 calBP) is exactly tied, so the safest phrasing is a peak spanning 1400-1201 BCE, best single century 1300-1201 BCE, which wins outright under 150/200/250-year smoothing (3 of 5 windows) and is identical in capital.csv, the raw anchors of time_series_data.csv and its annual interpolated grid. The individual social-capital components that increase are Copper & Gold (ZCU_AU: Z=+2.54, 95th percentile, 59.9% of the peak anomaly, positive 500-year trend) and Monument Count (ZMonument: Z=+1.71, 97th percentile, 40.3% of the anomaly, positive trend); together they account for essentially 100% of the peak anomaly (+4.238 exact additive decomposition). Amber (Zamber) does NOT increase: Z=-0.01 at the peak, -0.3% of the anomaly, its own maximum lying in 3300-3000 BCE with a negative long-run trend. The peak is social-specific in the 13th-century bin: cultural capital (pottery form/decoration diversity) is below its mean (28th of 39 bins) and economic capital (Depot, Sickle, Axes & Celts, Monument Size) is below its mean (34th of 39), while only symbolic capital (Hatchets & Swords, Daggers, House Size) is simultaneously high (2nd of 39) although its own maximum lies two centuries later (1800-1701 BCE); in the tied 14th-century bin economic capital is also elevated, so the 'social only' reading is strongest for 1300-1201 BCE. We therefore interpret the peak as a metallurgical plus monumental-construction phenomenon - prestige copper/gold deposition and collective labour mobilisation - rather than an across-the-board prosperity maximum or a long-distance exchange boom, since amber, the exchange proxy, is decoupled from it. Landscape openness/demography (Belau/Woserin pollen PC1) correlates only weakly (r = 0.02-0.32, n = 36 overlapping bins) and is explicitly not claimed as the mechanism.
payload.workflow: Read capital.csv with decimal=',' (39 x 100-year bins, BCE positive, no NaN) as the primary grid and sorted chronologically; built SC = ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument (simple sum of raw Z) plus two sensitivity variants (mean of the 3, re-standardised sum); scanned the argmax century with 50/100/150/200/250-year centered rolling means (50y = 2 bins ... 250y = 5 bins) and reported ties explicitly; built a stability table for SC and for the symbolic/cultural/economic blocks. Applied the pre-registered component rule (>=2 of: >=25% of the peak anomaly, delta vs series mean >= +0.5 Z, positive slope over the preceding 500 years) to all 12 components at BOTH tied peak bins, using the exact additive decomposition of the sum for the % of anomaly, and suppressing percentages when a block anomaly was <= +0.5. Compared the four capital blocks under the same sum rule at both tied bins (value, z-score, rank, percentile) to test whether the social peak is specific. Cross-checked the peak on time_series_data.csv using both the 37 raw 100-year anchors (identical to capital.csv, max abs diff 0) and the annual _inter grid with a tie-aware bin comparison. Ran an explicitly secondary pollen check on the 36-bin overlap (4300-800 BCE) against MEAN / Belau_PC1_inter / Woserin_PC1_inter / SMOOTH_MEAN_100y / SMOOTH_MEAN_250y with -200..+200-year lags, using only the fully populated interpolated columns (raw pollen / raw PC1, ~95% NaN, never used). calBP = 1950 - CE_signed. No matplotlib in the environment, so section G prints ASCII panels and writes output/summary.json instead of a PNG.
